title: The Lion and the Hare
blurb: The smallest hare in the forest walks up the hill alone.
script:
[warmly] In a forest of tall green trees… there lived a lion who believed he was the greatest thing that had ever lived.

[grandly] Every morning he roared so loudly that the birds forgot their songs and the leaves shook on their branches. [gently] And every day he hunted… far more than he could eat.

[worried] So the animals held a meeting under the old banyan tree.

[sadly] “He takes ten of us a day,” said the deer, “and eats only one.”

[thoughtful] The old owl blinked slowly. “Then let us make him an offer,” she said. “One animal each day. Sent to him. And he must hunt no more.”

[calmly] And to everyone's surprise… the lion agreed.

[softly] And so it began. Each morning, one animal walked up the hill to the lion's den. [sadly] And each morning, the forest grew a little quieter.

[short pause] Until one day… it was the turn of the smallest hare of all.

[curious] Now the hare did not run. He did not cry. [playfully] He set off up the hill… very… slowly.

[amused] He stopped to smell a flower. He watched a beetle climb a stone. He sat down for a while and thought about things. [cheerfully] The sun climbed high in the sky before he came anywhere near the lion.

[angry] “You are LATE!” the lion roared, and the whole hill shook.

[calmly] “Forgive me, great one,” said the hare, and he bowed. “I set out early. Truly I did. [worried] But on the road… I met another lion.”

[surprised] The lion's tail went stiff. “Another… lion?”

[softly] “He stopped me,” said the hare. “He said HE was the greatest in this forest. He said your name… and he laughed.”

[excited] Well. The lion was on his feet at once.

[grandly] “SHOW ME,” he said. “Take me to him NOW.”

[playfully] So the hare led him down through the ferns, past the banyan tree, to an old stone well that stood in the long grass.

[quietly] “He lives down there,” whispered the hare. “Deep down. That is his home.”

[curious] The lion put his great paws on the wall of the well… and leaned over… and looked down into the dark water.

[loudly] And a lion looked back at him! [excited] He roared — and the other lion roared! He showed his teeth — and the other showed his teeth!

[dramatic] So he jumped in… to fight him. [short pause] And he was never seen again.

[warmly] And the little brown hare walked home through the ferns, [amused] and by evening the forest was full of songs. [long pause] [whispers] The smallest one… had saved them all.
